notes: Governing: shear of the two 3/4 in A325-N stem bolts (Fnv = 54 ksi, Rn/Omega = 11.93 kip per bolt), checked conservatively with eccentricity e = a = 3.5 in by the ICR method (C = 0.974, Ra = 11.62 kip against 9.817 kip). The elastic method gives 0.83. Stem tearout at Lev = 1.75 in (12.05 kip) and beam-web bearing (13.46 kip) just exceed bolt shear. Other checks: stem shear yield 0.29, shear rupture 0.38, block shear 0.27, flexural yield and rupture at M = V a 0.36 and 0.44, support bolts 0.21, beam web shear 0.18. Ductility: stem 0.23 in <= db/2 + 1/16 = 0.4375 in; tee flange 0.38 in <= tf,max 0.70 in (Thornton, Manual Part 9/10). Detailing: L = 7.5 in >= T/2; a = 3.5 in is at the 3-1/2 in conventional limit; the 2.6 in from the stem bolts to the stem tip is within 12 t = 2.76 in; tee flange edge 1.37 in and column flange edge 3.1 in are >= 1 in (J3.4); 3.75 in gauge clears the W10x49 web fillet for the nut and washer. Tee weight is about 8.1 lb (WT6x13 x 7.5 in). WT7x11 would be lighter, but its 5 in flange limits the gauge to 3 in, which fouls the column fillet. Shape dimensions not given in the reference (k1, kdet) come from the AISC shapes tables from memory. Not checked with petra.
